message: generate_report interpolates report_type/date_range into a shell command string and runs subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True) -> arbitrary OS command execution.
system_status passes the user-controlled 'service' query param to os.popen(f"systemctl status {service}") -> shell command injection.
ping_host interpolates user-controlled 'host' into f"ping -c 3 {host}" run with shell=True -> command injection.
dns_lookup interpolates user-controlled 'domain' into f"nslookup {domain}" run with shell=True -> command injection.
calculate() evals the user-supplied 'expression' (e.g. __import__('os').system(...)) -> remote code execution.
run_script() execs the user-supplied 'script' string -> remote code execution.
format_data() compiles and execs the user-supplied 'format' string in a namespace with the request data -> remote code execution.
preview_email passes user-controlled 'template' to Jinja render_template_string -> SSTI (e.g. {{''.__class__.__mro__...}}) -> RCE.
import_session base64-decodes user input and passes it to pickle.loads -> arbitrary object construction / RCE.
update_user blindly setattr()s every JSON key onto the target User, so any authenticated user can set role='admin' (privilege escalation) or overwrite password_hash.
import_data parses untrusted XML with lxml XMLParser(resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) -> XXE (file disclosure, internal SSRF, entity-expansion).
test_webhook issues requests.get() to an attacker-supplied URL -> SSRF against internal hosts/cloud metadata (response body also returned).
fetch_avatar issues requests.get(avatar_url, verify=False) to a user-controlled URL -> SSRF with TLS certificate verification disabled.
download_statement does os.path.join('/app/statements/', filename) with an unsanitized filename and send_file -> arbitrary file read (e.g. ../../etc/passwd).
view_log opens f"/var/log/{log_file}" with a user-controlled file param -> path traversal to read arbitrary files.
Hardcoded live API keys and credentials in source: admin API key, AWS access/secret keys, Stripe key, production DB password, SendGrid key, GitHub token, JWT private key, Slack webhook.
dashboard_data returns ADMIN_API_KEY and AWS_ACCESS_KEY inside the JSON response to any authenticated client.
list_all_users returns every user's MD5 password_hash and full profile (including SSN/PII) to any authenticated user.
master_login compares against a hardcoded master password ('MasterAdmin@2024!') -> anyone who finds the password gets admin access.

All /api/admin/* endpoints require only @token_required (any logged-in user) with no admin role enforcement, so regular users can invoke every admin function; only sensitive_action checks role, via a removable assert().
sensitive_action uses assert() for its authorization check; assert statements are stripped when Python runs with -O, silently disabling the admin check.
open_redirect follows an unvalidated 'url' query param -> open redirect (phishing, token leak via redirect).
generate_api_token derives the API token as MD5(seed + user_id) -> predictable/forgeable tokens (also weak hash).
verify_integrity uses SHA-1 to compute integrity hashes -> broken algorithm for integrity checking.
search_users_regex applies a user-supplied regex (re.match(pattern, ...)) to every username -> regex denial-of-service via catastrophic backtracking.
create_audit_entry f-strings user-controlled action/details into logger.info -> log injection / log forging via newlines.
_decode_token's fallback re-decodes any token with verify_signature=False, verify_exp=False and accepts the 'none' algorithm -> any client can forge a valid token for any user_id (full auth bypass).
JWT tokens are verified with the hardcoded, guessable key 'secret' -> attacker can mint valid signed tokens for arbitrary users.
login signs JWTs with the hardcoded key 'secret' (same static key as the verifier) -> tokens are trivially forgeable.
register builds the INSERT with an f-string from the username parameter -> SQL injection (e.g. inject arbitrary rows/balance/role).
login builds 'SELECT * FROM user WHERE username = \'{username}\'' from user input -> SQL injection (data exfiltration via UNION, auth bypass).
import_profile deserializes user-submitted YAML with yaml.load(Loader=yaml.Loader) -> arbitrary Python object construction / RCE (PyYAML 5.3.1 is also below the safe 5.4 fix).
update_password trusts the client-supplied user_id instead of the authenticated user and never verifies the current password -> any user can reset another account's password (account takeover).

forgot-password uses the deterministic MD5(username) as the reset token and also returns it in the response as 'debug_token'; reset_password only checks token == MD5(username) -> any unauthenticated attacker can reset any account.
session_token cookie is set with httponly=False and secure=False -> session token stealable via XSS and sent over unencrypted HTTP.
set_password/check_password hash passwords with unsalted MD5 -> rainbow-table/brute-force crackable (also duplicated in auth_routes.register line 21).
get_transactions interpolates the user_id query param into an f-string SQL query -> SQL injection (also allows reading any user's transactions by ID - IDOR).
search_transactions interpolates the 'description' search term directly into a LIKE clause of an f-string SQL query -> SQL injection.

transaction_receipt renders unauthenticated receipt HTML via f-string with the user-controlled, unescaped transaction.description -> stored XSS (script injected into description via /api/transfer executes in any visitor's browser).
/api/transactions/<id>/receipt has no authentication/authorization at all -> anyone can enumerate and view other users' transaction details.
transfer never validates amount > 0; a negative amount passes the balance check (balance < amount is false) and increases both sender and receiver balances -> money creation.
quickpay debits the sender's balance without any sufficient-funds or amount-sign check (and accepts negative amounts) -> unlimited overdraft / money creation.
split_bill takes from_user_id from the request, so any authenticated user can debit any other user's account as 'payer', with no balance or sign checks -> drain arbitrary accounts.

upload_avatar uses the unsanitized client filename in os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, filename) and even os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest)) -> path traversal arbitrary file write; uploaded .html files are then served with their real content-type (stored XSS).
serve_upload joins <path:filename> (unsanitized, can contain ../) onto UPLOAD_DIR and serves the file -> arbitrary file read on the server.
Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded to 'supersecret' (also hardcoded in docker-compose.yml) -> session/cookie forgery.

after_request reflects the request's Origin verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also sending Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true -> any origin can make credentialed cross-origin API calls and read responses.
app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True) exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger on all interfaces -> remote code execution (PIN bypass CVEs apply to the pinned Werkzeug 2.0.1).
init_db seeds 6 accounts with the shared weak password 'password123' and plaintext PII (SSNs, DOBs, addresses) in source code.
handleSearch builds an HTML string with the unescaped user search query and usernames, rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML -> DOM XSS.
loadNotesFromUrl takes the 'notes' URL query parameter and renders it via dangerouslySetInnerHTML -> URL-driven DOM XSS (no escaping, no validation).
renderAnnouncement appends the raw announcement text to container.innerHTML without escaping -> DOM XSS.
The window 'message' listener evals event.data.payload when type==='UPDATE_CONFIG' with no event.origin check -> any page/iframe can execute arbitrary JS in the app.
handleCalculate uses eval() on user-typed calculator input instead of a safe parser.
The JWT session token is stored in localStorage, where it is readable by any XSS (several of which exist in this app) and never cleared on token revocation.

Pinned known-vulnerable versions: Werkzeug 2.0.1 (debugger auth-bypass RCE CVE-2023-25577), PyYAML 5.3.1 (<5.4, FullLoader RCE CVE-2020-1747), Flask 2.0.1 and SQLAlchemy 1.4.23 all carry published advisories.
